como.cinturaHombre: Level with your navel, standing, belly relaxed. Measure at the end of a normal breath out, without sucking in.
como.cinturaMujer: At the narrowest point, between your navel and breastbone. If it isn’t clear, measure a few times and keep the smallest.
como.cuello: Just below the Adam’s apple, tape straight around the neck, chin forward, shoulders down. Snug: self-measured necks tend to read large.
como.cadera: At the widest part of your buttocks, seen from the side, feet together.
como.brazo: Halfway between the tip of your shoulder and your elbow, arm relaxed at your side.
como.pecho: At the middle of your breastbone, tape under your arms, after breathing out.
como.muslo: Halfway between the crease of your groin and the top of your kneecap.

consejos: A tape that doesn’t stretch, on bare skin.
Standing, feet together, arms at your sides, relaxed.
Keep the tape level with the floor: a mirror helps.
At the end of a normal breath out: don’t suck in.
Always at the same time of day, before eating and after the bathroom.
Measure twice; if they differ by more than 1 cm, a third time, and write down the average.
cuerpo.usaHombre: The estimate uses your waist and neck, with your height. The other measurements help you follow your progress.
cuerpo.usaMujer: The estimate uses your waist, hips and neck, with your height. The other measurements help you follow your progress.
cuerpo.aviso: This is an estimate from your measurements, not a measurement: a lab scan (DEXA) could read 3 or 4 points higher or lower. It’s less precise with very little fat, a lot of muscle or a lot of fat, and it doesn’t apply during pregnancy or under 18. Measure the same way every time and watch the trend.
cuerpo.comoSeEstimaHombre: With the US Navy method (Hodgdon and Beckett, 1984): body density comes from your waist minus your neck and your height, and body fat from the Siri equation. The range is the estimate plus and minus how much it changes if the tape shifts 1 cm at the waist and half a centimetre at the neck, rounded to whole points. With very little or a lot of fat, it opens one more point on each side.
cuerpo.comoSeEstimaMujer: With the US Navy method (Hodgdon and Beckett, 1984): body density comes from your waist plus your hips minus your neck and your height, and body fat from the Siri equation. The range is the estimate plus and minus how much it changes if the tape shifts 1 cm at the waist and hips and half a centimetre at the neck, rounded to whole points. With very little or a lot of fat, it opens one more point on each side.

textos.llegaste: You reached your goal weight. To stay there, switch your goal to maintain.

textos.alReves: Your trend is going the other way ({ritmo} {unidad} a week). The weekly check-in adjusts your targets for that.
textos.estable: Your trend moves less than 150 g a week: you’re maintaining.

progreso.cinturaAltura: Waist-to-height: {n}. The UK NICE guideline recommends under 0.5.
progreso.medidasDel: Measured on {fecha}; the change is against a month earlier.
progreso.comoSeCalculaTexto: Over the last {dias} days you ate {promedio} kcal a day on average and your trend changed {cambio} {unidad}. Moss takes a quarter of the difference from its previous estimate, so your target changes gradually.
progreso.ritmoTexto: {pct}% of your weight a week: about {kg} {unidad}.
progreso.objetivoNota: When you change your goal, your targets change from today, using the expenditure Moss has been measuring.
progreso.pesoMetaNota: It shows whether you’re on track and when you’d get there. Targets come from your goal and pace.
progreso.controlListo: The week already has what it needs: the check-in will measure your expenditure and adjust your targets.
progreso.controlFalta: The check-in needs at least 4 logged days and one weigh-in in the week. Without them, your targets stay as they are.
progreso.diaDelControlNota: That day, when you open Moss, the check-in measures the week before. If you don’t open the app that day, it runs next time.
progreso.controlTexto: The check-in measured an expenditure of about {gasto} kcal a day. Moss takes it in gradually: the estimate went from {antes} to {ahora} kcal.

metas.mossTexto: Moss adjusts them every week from your weight and what you eat.
metas.aManoTexto: You set them. Moss keeps measuring your expenditure, but doesn't change them.

equilibrada: Protein by body weight, at least 27% fat and the rest carbs.
bajaEnGrasas: Fat at 20%: more room for carbs.
bajaEnCarbohidratos: A quarter of calories from carbs and the rest from fat.

metas.semanaTexto: More on the days you pick and a bit less on the rest. The week adds up the same: carbs move.

progreso.controlEnCurso: The check-in needs at least 4 logged days and one weigh-in in the week. There are {n} days left: if you keep logging, that’s enough.
progreso.ejemplo: This is sample data: once you log your weight (or connect Health) and finish the questionnaire, yours shows up.
progreso.sinMedidas: No measurements yet. With your waist and neck (and hips, for women), Moss estimates your body fat.
progreso.gastoInicial: Estimated from your answers. Each weekly check-in measures it from your weight and what you eat.

sueno.horas: Fell asleep at {desde}, woke up at {hasta}
sueno.incompleta: This night looks incomplete: you slept much less than usual and woke up early. Did your watch run out of battery? You can leave it out.
sueno.etapasEstimadas: Stages are the watch’s estimate: it gets them right much less often than how long you slept.
sueno.sinRelojTexto: Your watch didn’t record this night (out of battery, or not wearing it?). There’s only the iPhone’s time in bed, which measures phone use, not sleep: it doesn’t count for anything.
sueno.sinNadaTexto: There’s no data for this night. It isn’t filled in: it stays out of averages and debt.
sueno.habitosPendientes: That day’s sleep habits stay pending: you can mark them yourself.
sueno.sinCalidad: Without the watch there’s no quality: it needs to know how long you slept.
comoCalidad: It’s a Moss number, from 0 to 100, in three parts. It isn’t Apple’s Sleep Score: Apple doesn’t share it with other apps, so they may not match.
Duration (50): how long you slept against what you need ({necesidad}). 4 hours scores 0, and reaching it scores 50.

Timing (30): how far your sleep and wake times moved from your usual ones (the median of your last two weeks). Up to half an hour scores everything; an hour and a half or more, nothing. With fewer than 5 nights it’s left out and the total is rescaled.
Continuity (20): minutes awake between falling asleep and waking up (full up to 20, none from 60) and awakenings of 5 minutes or more (full with one, none with four).
Stages, time in bed and heart rate aren’t included: the watch measures them less accurately.
sueno.regularidadTexto: From {n} of the last 14 nights. The ± is how much your time moves from night to night: up to half an hour is very regular. The weekend compares the middle of your Friday and Saturday nights with the rest, assuming you don’t work those days.
sueno.deudaDe: short of what you need ({necesidad} a night)
sueno.deudaTexto: What you were short of what you need each night over the last two weeks, counting recent nights more, minus what you slept extra (up to 2 hours a night). Naps count; nights without data neither add nor subtract.
sueno.vitalesTexto: The average while you slept, against the median of your previous nights (7 are needed). The watch measures variability only a few times a night: it’s the least precise. Resting heart rate is for the whole day.
sueno.fuentesTexto: Moss uses a single source per night: the one you choose or, if not, your watch, then another device, and the phone last. It never adds two together. If a night is missing, it stays grey: nothing is made up.
sueno.noMedico: Moss isn’t a medical device. If you’re worried about your sleep, talk to a doctor.
sueno.ejemplo: These are sample nights: once you connect Health, yours show up.

perfil.borrarDatosTexto: Your habits, food log, weight, measurements and targets are deleted, on this phone and in your account. The account stays, and Ascent isn’t touched.
perfil.borrarCuentaTexto: Your account is the same in Moss and Ascent: deleting it deletes the data of both, and it can’t be undone.
perfil.cerrarSesionTexto: What’s on this phone is deleted; your data stays in your account.
perfil.errorBorrar: That didn’t work. Check your connection and try again.
perfil.exportarTexto: Each file is a CSV that any spreadsheet opens.
perfil.tusDatosNota: Changing your details doesn’t change your targets: each weekly check-in measures what you really burn.

fuentes.off: Products: Open Food Facts, under the ODbL
fuentes.estrellas: Stars: Yale Bright Star Catalogue (Hoffleit and Warren, 1991; CDS) and IAU star names (WGSN, CC BY 4.0)

privacidadTexto: Your data is yours. Moss keeps it on your phone and, with your account, on its server to sync it; it doesn’t sell or share it.
What it reads from Health (steps, sleep, water, mindfulness, weight) stays on your phone and only lights your habits and fills in your details. Moss doesn’t write to Health.
Food photos stay on your phone. When you scan a code that isn’t in Moss, only that code is looked up on Open Food Facts.
You can export everything as CSV and delete your data or your account from here.

hoy.reparto: Gym days get {entreno} kcal and rest days {descanso}. The week adds up to {semana}, the same as the check-in.

proteina.techo: Protein stays: it’s already at 2.2 g per kilo, and more doesn’t add muscle.
proteina.chica: Protein stays: the session was half your usual or less.

recuperacion.texto: A daily score from your sleep, your food and your training. Before you train, it tells you whether to go hard or easy.
recuperacion.explicacion: Sleep, 40: how much you slept against what you need, and the night’s quality. Load, 40: what you trained in the previous 3 days against your 4-week average, minus days in a row. Food, 20: yesterday’s protein and whether you ate at least 80% of your target. It’s a guide.

estancamiento.texto: When Ascent sees you’ve stalled on an exercise, Moss adds what changed in your sleep, protein and calories.

frases.sueno: Your best lifts come in the weeks you sleep {horas} or more.
frases.proteina: Your best lifts come in the weeks you hit your protein.
frases.calorias: Your best lifts come in the weeks you eat closer to your expenditure.

estancamiento.nota: It’s a probable cause, not a sure one: it compares your weeks.
estancamiento.juntando: Moss is still gathering information to find the probable cause.
estancamiento.juntandoDetalle: It needs {min} weeks with PRs and {min} without, each with at least {dias} days of food and {dias} nights of sleep. So far, {a} and {b}.
estancamiento.sinDiferencia: There’s no clear difference in your sleep, protein or calories: the probable cause lies elsewhere.
